import Mathlib

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def insertionSort_precond (v : List Int) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  True
  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
/-- Insert `x` into the (already sorted) list `l`, keeping it sorted. -/
def insertOrdered (x : Int) : List Int → List Int
  | [] => [x]
  | y :: ys => if x ≤ y then x :: y :: ys else y :: insertOrdered x ys

/-- Recursive insertion sort: sort the tail, then insert the head. -/
def insertionSortAux : List Int → List Int
  | [] => []
  | x :: xs => insertOrdered x (insertionSortAux xs)
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definitions
def insertionSort (v : List Int) (h_precond : insertionSort_precond v) : List Int :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  insertionSortAux v
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def insertionSort_postcond (v : List Int) (result : List Int) (h_precond : insertionSort_precond v) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
   List.Sorted (· ≤ ·) result ∧ result.Perm v
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
theorem insertOrdered_perm (x : Int) (l : List Int) :
    (insertOrdered x l).Perm (x :: l) := by
  induction l with
  | nil => simp [insertOrdered]
  | cons y ys ih =>
    by_cases hxy : x ≤ y
    · simp [insertOrdered, hxy]
    · simp only [insertOrdered, hxy, if_false]
      exact (ih.cons y).trans (List.Perm.swap x y ys)

theorem insertOrdered_sorted (x : Int) (l : List Int) (h : List.Sorted (· ≤ ·) l) :
    List.Sorted (· ≤ ·) (insertOrdered x l) := by
  induction l with
  | nil => simp [insertOrdered]
  | cons y ys ih =>
    obtain ⟨hy, hys⟩ := List.sorted_cons.mp h
    by_cases hxy : x ≤ y
    · simp only [insertOrdered, hxy, if_true]
      rw [List.sorted_cons]
      refine ⟨?_, h⟩
      intro b hb
      rcases List.mem_cons.mp hb with rfl | hb
      · exact hxy
      · exact le_trans hxy (hy b hb)
    · simp only [insertOrdered, hxy, if_false]
      rw [List.sorted_cons]
      refine ⟨?_, ih hys⟩
      intro b hb
      rcases List.mem_cons.mp ((insertOrdered_perm x ys).mem_iff.mp hb) with rfl | hb
      · exact le_of_not_le hxy
      · exact hy b hb

theorem insertionSortAux_perm (l : List Int) : (insertionSortAux l).Perm l := by
  induction l with
  | nil => simp [insertionSortAux]
  | cons x xs ih =>
    exact (insertOrdered_perm x (insertionSortAux xs)).trans (ih.cons x)

theorem insertionSortAux_sorted (l : List Int) : List.Sorted (· ≤ ·) (insertionSortAux l) := by
  induction l with
  | nil => simp [insertionSortAux]
  | cons x xs ih => exact insertOrdered_sorted x (insertionSortAux xs) ih
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem insertionSort_postcond_satisfied (v : List Int) (h_precond : insertionSort_precond v) :
    insertionSort_postcond v (insertionSort v h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  exact ⟨insertionSortAux_sorted v, insertionSortAux_perm v⟩
  -- !benchmark @end proof

What's in `Solution.lean`:

- **auxcode**: `insertOrdered x l` walks the sorted list and places `x` before the first element ≥ it; `insertionSortAux` sorts the tail recursively then inserts the head — standard recursive insertion sort.
- **code**: `insertionSortAux v`.
- **lemma**: four lemmas — `insertOrdered` produces a permutation of `x :: l`, preserves sortedness (using the permutation lemma to characterize membership in the recursive branch), and the two corresponding facts lifted to `insertionSortAux` by list induction.
- **proof**: pairs the two `insertionSortAux` lemmas.

Only warnings remain (unused binders, plus `le_of_not_le` being deprecated in favor of `le_of_not_ge`).
